meta.titre: French Articles: le, un, du, au and when to use de
meta.sous_theme: Definite, indefinite and partitive articles, contractions and negation

sections.contenu_markdown: Imagine a seller at a market stall who asks a customer: *Vous voulez du riz ou des haricots ?* Two tiny words, *du* and *des*, tell the customer that the seller is offering some rice and some beans, not one particular bag. French needs an article before almost every noun, and the choice changes with the meaning, the gender, the number and even the words that come before. That is why a gap before a noun is one of the commonest questions in Paper 1, and why it is easy to win these marks with a short method.

items: Every French noun is masculine or feminine, and singular or plural.
Before a vowel or a mute h, *le* and *la* become *l'* (*l'école*, *l'huile*).
The prepositions *à* and *de* can stand in front of an article (*à la maison*, *de la ville*).

sections.titre: Articles: three kinds, four contractions, and the rule of de
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The three kinds of article

| Kind | Forms | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Definite | le, la, l', les | a particular thing, or a thing in general (tastes, truths) | *Le riz est cuit.* *J'aime le riz.* (I like rice.) |
| Indefinite | un, une, des | one or several things, not specified | *J'achète un poulet.* (I buy a chicken.) |
| Partitive | du, de la, de l' | an amount of something that is not counted | *Je mange du riz.* *Elle boit de l'eau.* |

Use *l'* before a vowel or a mute h: *l'huile*, *de l'huile*, *l'école*.

### Contractions with à and de

à + le = **au**, à + les = **aux**, de + le = **du**, de + les = **des**. Nothing changes with *la* and *l'*: *à la maison*, *de l'école*. *Il va au marché. Elle revient des champs.* The forms *à le*, *à les*, *de le* and *de les* never exist.

### When the article becomes de

After a **negation**, *un, une, des, du, de la, de l'* become **de** (**d'** before a vowel): *Je n'ai pas de pain. Il n'y a plus d'eau.* The definite article does not change (*Je n'aime pas le riz*), and after *être* in the negative *un, une, des* stay (*Ce n'est pas un livre*).

After a word of **quantity** (*beaucoup de, trop de, assez de, peu de, un kilo de, une bouteille de*) use **de** with no article: *beaucoup de bananes, un kilo de sucre.*

### Choosing on the exam

1. Look at the noun: gender, number, vowel or consonant at the start.
2. Look before the gap: *à*, *de*, a negation, a quantity word?
3. Decide the idea: general fact or taste (definite), a specific or counted item (indefinite), an amount of something uncountable (partitive).
4. Read the sentence with your choice.

variantes.nom: The definite article for tastes, countries and the body
variantes.quand_utiliser: After verbs of liking, with names of countries, days, languages, and parts of the body
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use the definite article for what is liked or disliked in general: *J'aime le manioc. Je déteste les mensonges.* Countries take an article: *le Cameroun, la France, les États-Unis.* A day with the article means *every*: *le lundi* (on Mondays). Parts of the body take the definite article, not a possessive: *Il a mal à la tête. Il a mal aux dents. Elle se lave les mains. Ferme les yeux.*

variantes.nom: The partitive and expressions of quantity
variantes.quand_utiliser: For food, drink and uncountable things such as noise, luck or wind
variantes.contenu_markdown: *Du, de la, de l'* mean *some*: *Il mange du pain. Elle met de la sauce. Je bois de l'eau.* Abstract and uncountable words follow the same rule: *Il y a du bruit. Elle a de la chance. Il fait du vent.* With a word of quantity or after *sans*, drop the article: *beaucoup d'eau, trop de bruit, un café sans sucre.* Note the elision before a vowel: *beaucoup d'eau*, not *beaucoup de eau*.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must choose between le and la, un and une, and the noun is not obvious
variantes.contenu_markdown: Endings help. Most nouns in **-tion, -sion, -té** are feminine (*la nation, la solution, la santé*), with exceptions such as *le côté* and *l'été*. Most nouns in **-age, -ment, -eau** are masculine (*le village, le moment, le bateau*); exceptions: *la plage, la page, la cage, l'image, la nage, l'eau, la peau*. Learn each food noun with its article: *le pain, le sel, le poisson, le plantain, la farine, la viande, l'huile (f.), l'arachide (f.)*.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Choose the correct form for each gap.

1. Ma tante vend ____ poissons frais.
   A) du   B) des   C) de la   D) au
2. Il n'y a plus ____ sel dans la cuisine.
   A) du   B) le   C) de   D) des
3. Les enfants vont ____ marché avec leur père.
   A) à le   B) au   C) du   D) à la
4. Elle boit beaucoup ____ eau chaque jour.
   A) de l'   B) d'   C) de la   D) l'

etapes.justification: The article depends on gender, number and the first letter.
etapes.resultat_markdown: *Poissons*: masculine plural. *Sel*: masculine singular, starts with a consonant. *Marché*: masculine singular. *Eau*: feminine singular, starts with a vowel.

etapes.action: Look for a trigger before the gap.
etapes.justification: A negation or a word of quantity changes the article to *de*. A preposition may need a contraction.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Q2: *il n'y a plus* (negation). Q3: the verb *vont* needs *à*. Q4: *beaucoup* (quantity). Q1: no trigger.

etapes.justification: Q1 names an unspecified plural group: indefinite plural *des*. Q2 is negative, so *de* and no article. Q4 follows *beaucoup*, so *de*, which becomes *d'* before the vowel of *eau*.
*À* + *le marché* gives *au marché*. The form *à le* does not exist.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The completed sentences are: **1** *Ma tante vend des poissons frais.* (My aunt sells fresh fish.) **2** *Il n'y a plus de sel dans la cuisine.* (There is no more salt in the kitchen.) **3** *Les enfants vont au marché avec leur père.* **4** *Elle boit beaucoup d'eau chaque jour.* (She drinks a lot of water every day.)

items.pourquoi_faux: After a negation, the indefinite article *des* becomes *de*.
items.correction_markdown: *Je n'ai pas **de** frères.* (I have no brothers.)

items.pourquoi_faux: The preposition *à* joins with *le* to form *au*. The form *à le* does not exist.
After a word of quantity such as *beaucoup*, the article is replaced by *de*.
items.correction_markdown: *Elle mange beaucoup **de** riz.* (She eats a lot of rice.)

items.pourquoi_faux: Verbs of liking and disliking speak of the thing in general, so they take the definite article, not the partitive.
*Huile* is feminine and starts with a mute h, so the partitive is *de l'*.

items.enonce_markdown:
Choose the correct form.

1. Nous allons ____ école à pied.
   A) au   B) à la   C) à l'   D) aux
2. Ma mère achète ____ lait pour le bébé.
   A) de   B) du   C) des   D) de la
items.solution_markdown:
1. *École* is feminine and starts with a vowel, so *à + l'école*. Answer **C**: *Nous allons à l'école à pied.* (We go to school on foot.)

2. *Lait* is masculine, uncountable and not negative: partitive *du*. Answer **B**: *Ma mère achète du lait pour le bébé.* (My mother buys some milk for the baby.)

items.enonce_markdown:
Write the missing word or words (choose among de, d', du, des, aux, au).

1. Je ne mange jamais ____ viande.
2. Il y a trop ____ bruit dans la salle.
3. Les élèves ont mal ____ pieds après la marche.
4. Nous parlons ____ enfants du quartier.
items.solution_markdown:
1. After the negation *ne ... jamais*, the partitive becomes *de*; *viande* starts with a consonant. Answer: **de**. *Je ne mange jamais de viande.* (I never eat meat.)

2. *Trop* is a word of quantity, so *de* with no article. Answer: **de**. *Il y a trop de bruit dans la salle.*

3. *Avoir mal à* + *les pieds* gives *aux pieds*. Answer: **aux**. *Les élèves ont mal aux pieds après la marche.* (The pupils have sore feet after the walk.)

4. *Parler de* + *les enfants* gives *des enfants*. Answer: **des**. *Nous parlons des enfants du quartier.* (We are talking about the children of the neighbourhood.)

items.enonce_markdown:
Translate into French.

1. I do not drink milk in the morning.
2. Marie sells bread and eggs.
3. He has a headache.
4. We need a lot of water.
items.solution_markdown:
1. *Boire du lait* becomes negative, so the partitive turns into *de*; the morning in general takes *le*. Answer: **Je ne bois pas de lait le matin.**

2. Unspecified amounts: *du pain* (partitive, masculine, uncountable) and *des œufs* (indefinite plural). Answer: **Marie vend du pain et des œufs.**

3. *Avoir mal à* + a body part with the definite article: *à la tête*. Answer: **Il a mal à la tête.**

4. *Avoir besoin de* followed by a quantity: *beaucoup d'eau*. Answer: **Nous avons besoin de beaucoup d'eau.**

items_markdown: Definite articles (*le, la, l', les*) name a particular thing or speak in general; indefinite articles (*un, une, des*) introduce unspecified things; partitive articles (*du, de la, de l'*) give an amount of something uncountable.
Contractions are compulsory: *à + le = au*, *à + les = aux*, *de + le = du*, *de + les = des*.
After a negation and after a word of quantity, *un, une, des, du, de la, de l'* become *de* (*d'* before a vowel): *pas de pain, beaucoup d'eau*.
Verbs of liking take the definite article (*J'aime le riz*); parts of the body take it too (*mal à la tête*).
Check the gender and the first letter of the noun before you choose, and read the whole sentence with your answer.
